def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tens:
## Definition

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.
thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordi:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.
thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.
thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-fre:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Second Bianchi identity.** For all indices $a,b,c,d,e$,
$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$
Equivalently, the antisymmetrization over the last three slots vanishes:
$R^a{}_{b[cd;e]}=0$.

**(b) Contracted identities.** $\nabla^a\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
=\tfrac12\nabla_bS$, and consequently
$$\nabla^aG_{ab}=0\qquad\text{for every }b,$$
where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing
of the contracted divergence for each second index; it does not assert that
all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.
def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instan:
## Definition

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$ be its curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be an affinely parametrized
geodesic with $D_s\gamma'=0$, written $T:=\gamma'$
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]); the parameter is the affinely
parametrized one of that definition and need not be proper time.

**(a) Fields along $\gamma$ and the derivative $D_s$.** A **field along
$\gamma$** is a section $J$ of the pullback bundle $\gamma^*TM$, and $D_s$
denotes the covariant derivative along $\gamma$ of
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. A field is **smooth** when its
coefficients in a smooth local frame of $M$ around each point of $\gamma$ are
$C^\infty$ on the corresponding parameter interval. At an included endpoint
of $I$ all derivatives below are one-sided.

**(b) Jacobi field.** A **Jacobi field along $\gamma$** is a smooth field $J$
along $\gamma$ satisfying the **Jacobi equation**
$$D_s^2J=R(T,J)T\qquad(s\in I),$$
that is $D_s^2J=R(\gamma',J)\gamma'$. The assignment
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$, which associates with a field along $\gamma$ another
field along $\gamma$ and is $\mathbb R$-linear, is the **Jacobi operator of
$\gamma$**. Whether the field is smooth only piecewise is stated whenever a
statement uses piecewise fields; the unqualified term means globally smooth.

**(c) Geodesic variations.** A **geodesic variation with affine
parameter $s$** is a smooth map $F:J_0\times I\to M$, where
$J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval with nonempty interior, such that
for every $r\in J_0$ the curve $s\mapsto F(r,s)$ is a geodesic with affine
parameter $s$. Its **variation field** is the field $s\mapsto\partial_rF(r,s)$
along the curve $s\mapsto F(0,s)$. The variation field of a geodesic
variation is a Jacobi field along that curve
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c)).

**(d) Conjugate instants and multiplicity.** Let $s_0<s_1$ be points of $I$.
The event $\gamma(s_1)$ is **conjugate to** $\gamma(s_0)$ **along $\gamma$**
when there is a nonzero Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$J(s_0)=J(s_1)=0$. In that case $s_1$ is called a **conjugate instant** of
$\gamma$ (with respect to $s_0$, when the base point needs to be named), and
the **multiplicity** of the conjugate instant is the dimension of the real
vector space of Jacobi fields vanishing at $s_0$ and $s_1$; the fields
vanishing at $s_0$ form a $4$-dimensional space and the multiplicity is at
most $4$, since a Jacobi field is determined by its value and derivative at
$s_0$ ([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (d)). For a
geodesic with $\gamma(s_0)=p$ and $\gamma'(s_0)=v$, the corresponding
possibility of conjugacy is measured by the derivative of the exponential
map at $s_1v$
([[lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map]]); that equivalence is proved,
not assumed here. No conjugate instant is asserted to exist.

**(e) The normal bundle.** If $\gamma$ is future timelike with
$g(T,T)=-1$, define the **normal bundle** $N_\gamma$ to be the family of
smooth fields $J$ along $\gamma$ with $g(J,T)=0$, and write $|J|:=\sqrt{g(J,J)}$
for $J\in N_\gamma$. Then $N_\gamma$ is a rank-three subbundle of
$\gamma^*TM$, $g$ restricts to a positive definite inner product on each
fibre, and $D_s$ preserves $N_\gamma$, because
$\frac{d}{ds}g(J,T)=g(D_sJ,T)+g(J,D_sT)=g(D_sJ,T)$ with $D_sT=0$; these
statements are proved in [[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] clause
(b). The **normal component** of a field $V$ is
$V^\perp:=V-g(V,T)T$ when $g(T,T)=-1$.
thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-devi:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp=J-g(J,\gamma')\gamma'$ is again a Jacobi field along
$\gamma$.
lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $p\in M$,
let $\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain and
$\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$ the exponential map of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], and identify
$T_{h}(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ by the canonical isomorphism for every
$h\in T_pM$ ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(a) The differential in terms of Jacobi fields.** Let $v\in T_pM$, let
$s_1>0$ satisfy $s_1v\in\mathcal E_p$, and let $u\in T_pM$. Let
$\gamma:[0,s_1]\to M$, $\gamma(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ (well defined by star-shapedness
of $\mathcal E_p$), and let $J_u$ be the unique Jacobi field along
$\gamma$ with $J_u(0)=0$ and $D_tJ_u(0)=u$
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)). Then
$$d(\exp_p)_{tv}(tu)=J_u(t)\qquad(0\le t\le s_1);$$
in particular $d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}(s_1u)=J_u(s_1)$ and, in the special case
$s_1=1$, $v\in\mathcal E_p$, $d(\exp_p)_v(u)=J_u(1)$.

**(b) Conjugacy as a kernel condition.** With the notation of (a),
$d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ is injective if and only if no nonzero Jacobi field
along $\gamma$ vanishes at $t=0$ and at $t=s_1$. Moreover
$\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}=s_1\{u\in T_pM:J_u(s_1)=0\}$, so
$\dim\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ equals the multiplicity of the conjugate
instant $s_1$ whenever $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(c) Conjugate instants of a geodesic.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth
geodesic with $\gamma(0)=p$, and let $s_1>0$ with $s_1\in I$ and
$s_1\gamma'(0)\in\mathcal E_p$. Then $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to
$\gamma(0)=p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if $d(\exp_p)_{s_1\gamma'(0)}$ is
not injective.
lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let
$a<b$ and let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a smooth future timelike geodesic with
$g(T,T)=-1$, $T:=\gamma'$, such that no instant $s\in(a,b]$ is conjugate to
$a$ along $\gamma$ ([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]]). Let
$N_\gamma$ be the normal bundle of $\gamma$ (clause (e) there) with the
positive definite fibre metric $g$, and for continuous piecewise-$C^1$
normal fields $J,K$ vanishing at $a$ and $b$ define
$$I(J,K):=\int_a^b\Bigl(g(D_sJ,D_sK)+g\bigl(R(T,J)T,K\bigr)\Bigr)ds,$$
the integral being over the smooth pieces of $J$ and $K$; write $I(J):=I(J,J)$
and $|J|:=\sqrt{g(J,J)}$.

**(a) The Jacobi operator on the normal bundle.** For every normal field $J$
the field $C_T(J):=R(T,J)T$ is again normal, and $C_T$ is $g$-selfadjoint on
each fibre: $g(C_T(J),K)=g(J,C_T(K))$ for normal fields $J,K$.

**(b) Matrix form.** Let $E_1,E_2,E_3$ be a parallel $g$-orthonormal frame of
$N_\gamma$ (which exists), and write $J=\sum_iJ^iE_i$, $K=\sum_iK^iE_i$ with
smooth coefficients on the smooth pieces. Then
$g(D_sJ,D_sK)=\sum_i(J^i)'(K^i)'$ and
$g(R(T,J)T,K)=\sum_{i,j}J^jC^i{}_jK^i$ for the smooth symmetric coefficient
functions $C^i{}_j:=g(C_T(E_j),E_i)$, so that the matrix
$C(s)=\bigl(C^i{}_j(s)\bigr)_{i,j}$ is symmetric for every $s$ and
$$I(J,K)=\int_a^b\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_i(J^i)'(K^i)'+J^TCK\Bigr)ds .$$

**(c) Factorization.** Let $A:[a,b]\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ be the unique solution
of the initial-value problem
$$A''=CA,\qquad A(a)=0,\qquad A'(a)=I_3 .$$
Then $A(s)$ is invertible for every $s\in(a,b]$, the field
$\Theta(s):=A'(s)A(s)^{-1}$ is symmetric on $(a,b]$ with
$$\Theta'=C-\Theta^2,$$
and for every continuous piecewise-$C^1$ normal field $J$ vanishing at $a$
and $b$,
$$I(J)=\int_a^b\bigl|J'-\Theta J\bigr|^2ds, $$
where $|J'-\Theta J|^2:=\sum_i\bigl((J^i)'-\sum_j\Theta^i{}_jJ^j\bigr)^2$ in
the frame of (b). Consequently $I(J)\ge0$, and $I(J)=0$ if and only if
$J=0$; the index form is positive definite on the space of such fields.
thm-gr-conjugacy-and-local-timelike-maxi:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $b>0$ and
let $\gamma:[0,b]\to M$ be a smooth future timelike geodesic with
$g(T,T)=-1$, $T:=\gamma'$, $p:=\gamma(0)$, and suppose that no
$s\in(0,b]$ is a conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(a) Conjugacy and the exponential differential.** For every $s\in(0,b]$,
$\gamma(s)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if
$d(\exp_p)_{sT(0)}$ is not injective; consequently
$d(\exp_p)_{sT(0)}$ is invertible for every $s\in[0,b]$.

**(b) Local proper-time maximum.** Fix a finite family of charts
$(U_1,x_1),\dots,(U_m,x_m)$ whose domains cover $\gamma([0,b])$ and a
partition $0=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ with
$\gamma([s_{i-1},s_i])\subseteq U_i$ for each $i$. For $\delta>0$ call a
piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ **$C^1$-$\delta$-close to
$\gamma$ relative to this data** when $\alpha([s_{i-1},s_i])\subseteq U_i$
for every $i$ and, on the common refinement of the admissible partitions of
$\alpha$ and $\gamma$, the coordinate representatives satisfy
$$\sup\bigl\|x_i\circ\alpha-x_i\circ\gamma\bigr\|<\delta, \qquad \sup\bigl\|(x_i\circ\alpha)'-(x_i\circ\gamma)'\bigr\|<\delta$$
on each common open piece contained in $(s_{i-1},s_i)$. Then there exists
$\delta>0$ such that every piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike curve
$\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=p$ and $\alpha(b)=\gamma(b)$ that is
$C^1$-$\delta$-close to $\gamma$ relative to the fixed data satisfies
$$L_g(\alpha)\le b=L_g(\gamma),$$
with equality if and only if there is a piecewise-$C^1$ strictly increasing
surjection $\rho:[0,b]\to[0,b]$ with $\alpha=\gamma\circ\rho$; that is,
$\alpha$ is a strictly monotone reparametrization of $\gamma$.

**(c) The normal index form.** The normal index form of
[[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] on the space of piecewise-$C^1$
normal fields along $\gamma$ vanishing at $0$ and $b$ is positive definite.
lem-gr-algebraic-curvature-vanishing-cri:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Let
$R_p:(T_pM)^4\to\mathbb R$ be an **algebraic curvature tensor at $p$**: an
$\mathbb R$-multilinear map whose components $R_{abcd}$ in a basis
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]) satisfy
$$R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab},\qquad R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0$$
for all $a,b,c,d$. Suppose that for every timelike $T\in T_pM$, every
$J\in T_pM$ and every $W\in T_pM$,
$$R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d=0 .$$
Equivalently (by nondegeneracy of $g_p$), the **tidal operator**
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ is zero for every timelike $T$, where $R(T,J)T$ is the
vector with $g_p\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d$ for all $W$. Then
$R_p=0$.

pthm-gr-tidal-comparison.physical_scope: Smooth test-field regime of the classical general-relativistic framework: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection, ideal freely falling structureless test bodies whose worldlines are future timelike geodesics parametrized by proper time, and smooth one-parameter families of such worldlines. Excludes bodies with non-negligible self-gravity, self-force, spin, finite size or internal structure, non-geodesic motion, non-smooth or distributional matter and fields, quantum effects, and any comparison with measured data. Every conclusion is a conditional model deduction from the adopted postulates, not an observational claim.

pthm-gr-tidal-comparison:
## Statement

Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, and let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],

$R$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). All statements below
are deductions within the model so specified; they assert nothing about
nature.

**(a) Free-fall congruences.** A **free-fall congruence** of the model is a
smooth map $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times I\to M$, with
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior, such that for every
$r$ the curve $\gamma_r:=\gamma(\cdot,r)$ is a future timelike geodesic
parametrized by proper time: with $U_r:=\partial_s\gamma$,
$$g(U_r,U_r)=-c^2,\qquad \nabla_{U_r}U_r=0 .$$
By clause (ii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], each $\gamma_r$ is
a worldline the model assigns to an ideal freely falling massive test body
with the corresponding release data, and conversely every such worldline
arises this way.

**(b) Deviation equation (model deduction).** Let $\gamma$ be a free-fall
congruence and set $J:=\partial_r\gamma$. Then, along each $\gamma_r$, the
separation field satisfies
$$D_s^2J=R(U_r,J)U_r,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$. In particular the
relative four-acceleration of nearby free-fall worldlines of the model is
exactly the curvature term: it is $\mathbb R$-linear in $J$, vanishes when
$J=0$, is a tensorial (frame- and coordinate-independent) linear map at each
event, and contains no rest mass, charge or internal-structure parameter of
the bodies.

**(c) Flat comparison and the vanishing criterion.** If the curvature
vanishes on an open subset $O\subseteq M$, then every free-fall congruence
with worldlines in $O$ has $D_s^2J=0$ there: the model predicts no tidal
relative acceleration of freely falling test bodies in that region.
Conversely, if at an event $q$ the operator $J\mapsto R(U,J)U$ vanishes for
every future timelike $U$ and every $J\in T_qM$, then $R_q=0$; hence within
the model the tidal response of all free-fall congruences detects exactly the
curvature, and $R$ is the model's complete tidal field at every event.

**Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the stated
postulates and the cited mathematics. No observation, apparatus, measured
input or statistical inference is used; the item contains no empirical
premises, and the word "tidal" denotes the curvature term in the model's
deviation equation, not a measured force on any particular body.
